li_dev: Quick escalation from onboarding: intermittent 401s right after token mint, then immediate 429s on bulk embedding calls. This started when we switched to a 30s TTL token. Anyone seen a token -> throttle cascade?
emma_cs: sorry about that. Is your rollout spawning lots of parallel workers? Can you paste the token response and a couple of failing request logs?
li_dev: sanitized logs below:
```nPOST /auth/token -> 200 {token: "ey...", expires_in: 30}
POST /v1/embeddings -> 401 {error: "invalid_token"}
POST /v1/embeddings -> 429 {error: "rate_limit"} x 15
```
li_dev: we spawn 50 workers during warmup; each gets its own token.
harry_sre: pattern looks like an auth race + burst window. Two common causes: 1) clock skew or TTL rounding makes freshly minted tokens appear expired; 2) per-worker refreshes cause a fanout of auth handshakes that the rate limiter counts as a burst. How do you obtain tokens today?
li_dev: per-worker fetch at process start. No centralization.
sdk-qa: suggestions: add client-side token slack (treat token TTL - 5s), implement singleflight refresh, and limit init concurrency. Example lightweight flags we recommend:
```js
client.opts = {tokenGraceMs:5000, maxInitConcurrent:6, refreshCoalesceMs:150};
```
emma_cs: we can also temporarily increase your burst allowance for the account while you ramp. Want me to apply +3rps for 24h?
li_dev: yes please, that would reduce noise for tomorrow's staged rollout. Also any jitter best practices?
harry_sre: add randomized jitter (0-300ms) between worker startups and use a steady ramp (2-4 workers/sec). If using HTTP/2 reuse, watch for connection header caching when rotating tokens; if proxy caches initial auth header it can yield mid-request 401s.
quota-bot: @emma_cs increased tenant "arcwave" burst quota: +3 rps for 24 hours (chg-id: R-21077).
li_dev: implemented singleflight and reduced init concurrency. After 10 minutes 401s stopped and 429s dropped dramatically. We'll keep the grace and jitter for the next 48h. Thanks! :rocket:
emma_cs: great. I'll add this to your onboarding notes (short TTL token patterns + SDK flags) and mark the account as "ramping" for the renewals team.
harry_sre: follow-up: infra should log a helpful header when token rotation + connection reuse is suspected (e.g., `x-auth-rotation: stale`); I'll open an infra task.
li_dev: we'll share a short note on our token issuance cadence too.
